Developers can now install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7, just one week after the sixth beta was released. Here are the details.

Apple releases macOS 27 beta 7

Last Monday, Apple ended a three-week beta hiatus by releasing macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6, which introduced redesigned traffic light window control buttons. macOS 27 beta 6 abandons the flat red, yellow, and green circular buttons in favour of a Liquid Glass-esque (though really quite Aqua-like) effect for the minimise, maximise, and close buttons.

Aside from this change, macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 did not introduce any other user-facing features or improvements, suggesting Apple may be using the final few betas to squash bugs and improve performance and security ahead of its official launch.

macOS 27 Golden Gate will introduce a brand new Siri app with a revamped Siri AI. The system will also include an AI-powered new Shortcuts app that can accept natural language instructions to create shortcuts, as well as tools to create Safari extensions from prompts.

In addition, macOS 27 Golden Gate will add new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, and will restore windows and apps to use fixed-radius rounded corners. This reverses a change from macOS 26, which adjusted the corner radius based on the contents of each window or app's menu bar.

macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 has a build number of 26A5421a. We are poring through the new beta right now and will report on what we find in due course.

How to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click on the info icon next to Beta Updates
  • Select macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta from the dropdown in the top right
  • Click Done

Have you spotted any new features in today's macOS 27 Golden Gate beta release? Let us know in the comments.
